ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in the Financial Sector (AMLA/GwG) of 10 October 1997, SR 955.0, as amended; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.033.0); Swiss Federal Criminal Code SR 311.0, Articles 305bis and 305ter; FINMA Circular 2018/07 on KYC and money-laundering due diligence. UBO/Transparency: Swiss Code of Obligations SR 220, including the duties of stock corporations to maintain the shareholder register (Aktienbuch) and an internal register of beneficial owners, coupled with the Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of the Beneficial Owners (Transparency Act) adopted by the Swiss Federal Assembly on 22 June 2023, which establishes a central UBO register with government-only access and a 25% ownership/control threshold, pending the Federal Council entry-into-force order; implementing guidance issued by the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) under SR 955.0.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: Swiss companies must maintain an internal UBO register exposed solely to regulatory inspection; the future central transparency register will be accessible only to Swiss supervisory and enforcement authorities (MROS, FINMA, cantonal prosecution authorities, tax authorities), with no public search right.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and signatories against: (i) the consolidated Swiss sanctions and embargo list administered by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), aligning with UN Security Council and EU restrictive measures; (ii) the OFAC SDN List and Foreign Sanctions Evaders List; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) the UK OFSI consolidated list; and (v) adverse media, Interpol, and public arrest-warrant sources. PEP status is determined under Article 2a AMLA/GwG and FINMA Circular 2018/07, covering foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates, and triggers enhanced due diligence with mandatory source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation. Screening results, review dates, and trigger-event refreshes must be documented in a dedicated KYC file retained for at least ten years after termination of the business relationship, and refreshed at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Zentraler Firmenindex (official central business name index, portal zefix.admin.ch), in conjunction with the Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregister) and the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB / Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt) for mandatory publications
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to Article 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, the firm name must be truthful, not misleading, and not contrary to public interest. The principal registered name must be formulated in one of the four Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh) using the Latin alphabet. For a stock corporation, the legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (or the French 'SA' / Italian 'SA' equivalents) is mandatory. Foreign-script names (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) are admissible only as a secondary firm name or in transliterated Latin-script form, with the transliteration explained to the registry; purely fanciful names, acronyms, and coined words require an explanatory statement of meaning to satisfy the non-deception review, and the name must be compatible with the language of the canton of registered office.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'Sparkasse', 'Finanzgesellschaft', 'Banque' - reserved and requires FINMA banking license under the Federal Banking Act SR 952.0
'Versicherung', 'Insurance', 'Assurance' - reserved and requires FINMA insurance supervision license

'Swiss', 'Schweizer', 'Suisse', 'Eidgenossisch', 'Bundes', 'Helvetia', 'Confederatio' - restricted where they imply a state or public-law connection; prior authorization of the competent federal authority is required
'Fonds', 'Fund', 'Kapitalanlage' - reserved where activity relates to collective investment schemes under the CISA (SR 951.31)
'Trust', 'Fiduciaire', 'Treuhand' - can be misleading absent a licensed fiduciary institution and may trigger enhanced prudential review by cantonal authorities
'Revisionsstelle', 'Audit', 'Wirtschaftsprufer' - restricted to licensed audit firms under the Swiss Audit Oversight Act
'Amtlich', 'Staatlich', 'Municipal', 'Nationalbank' - prohibited as implying official state functions; rejected under Article 950 CO public-interest test
Country or geographic tokens such as 'China', 'Zug', 'Zurich' - admissible only where the true territorial connection exists and the name is not otherwise deceptive
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed firm name by the cantonal commercial register office, the applicant must file an administrative appeal within 30 days of notification with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (kantonale Aufsichtsbehoerde). The appeal should set out the legal and factual grounds for admissibility of the name under Article 950 CO. If the supervisory authority upholds the rejection, a further appeal may be lodged within 30 days with the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht, BVGer) in St. Gallen. A rejected name may be re-filed with corrective wording at any time without prejudice; a new name reservation must be obtained for any revised filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office without physical Swiss presence is not acceptable. The registered office must be a physical address in the canton of incorporation, permanently accessible during normal business hours, where official service of process, correspondence from the commercial register and tax authorities, and inspection of books and records can occur (Article 629 CO and Article 39 ff. of the Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance, SR 221.411). A serviced office or licensed registered-agent arrangement with dedicated physical mailbox, meeting rooms, and administrative staffing is permissible and standard for a non-licensed passive electronic components distributor; however, the arrangement must demonstrate real administrative presence and cannot be a letterbox-only address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low estimated 5-10% annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a non-licensed, low-risk passive components distributor with no suspicious transaction patterns. Unannounced visits are normally initiated by cantonal commercial register offices, cantonal tax authorities, or enforcement bodies upon complaint, MLRO notification, or indicators of fictitious substance such as a high density of shell companies at a single address; the inspection risk rises materially where UBOs are PEPs or high-risk foreign nationals, where payment rails deviate from standard Swift wire transfers, or where the registered address hosts more than an ordinary number of commercial register entries.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), StAR - Articles 620 to 763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV); Federal Act on the Amendment of the Swiss Civil Code (OR) and related notarization requirements
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of the registered office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons); for Zug: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug, Industriestrasse 16, 6300 Zug, Switzerland
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Deed and Articles of Association (Statuten) with public notarization, together with the Board of Directors' declaration as to paid-up capital, filed through the Swiss commercial register electronic system (eGRIS/eHandelsregister)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 fully subscribed; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash before registration (20% of the total nominal capital per Article 632 OR); the paid-up amount must be credited to a blocked bank escrow account (Sperrkonto) in the company's name held by a Swiss bank and released only upon registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the share subscription be and is hereby ratified, and that the Board acknowledges receipt of the paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 on the blocked escrow account at [Bank] pursuant to Article 632 OR. RESOLVED that the registered office be and is hereby established at [Address], Zug, Switzerland, and that the corresponding Commercial Register filing be approved. RESOLVED that [Name A] is appointed Chairperson and Delegate, [Name B] Secretary, and [Name C] Money-Laundering Officer, each with individual signature authority (Einzelunterschrift). The Board is authorized to execute all registration filings, open the company's bank accounts, and correct any matters raised by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize the Foundation Deed and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public competent in the canton of registered office (e.g., Notariat und Grundbuchamt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present shareholders' passports, proof of address, and draft Articles of Association to the notary. The notary verifies the corporate name, object (distribution of passive electronic components under ISIC 4652), registered office, share capital, share classes, and board composition. All shareholders must sign the deed in person or by executed written power of attorney. The Articles of Association must specify the commercial purpose and capital structure in accordance with OR 626-628.
required_dossiers: Passport or identity document of each shareholder and director
Proof of residential address of each shareholder and director
Drafted Articles of Association (Statuten)
Certificate of name reservation from the Commercial Register (Name Reservation / Zefix)
Power of attorney if a shareholder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or Commercial Register queries the proposed name or purpose, obtain a revised name reservation and amend the Articles of Association by notarial deed; resubmit within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-Up Capital in a Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or licensed securities dealer; in Zug typical: Zuger Kantonalbank or UBS/ Credit Suisse private banking desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of the Aktiengesellschaft in formation and deposit at least CHF 50,000. The bank must issue a written confirmation that the capital is irrevocably placed under restriction. The escrow instruction must permit release only after the Commercial Register confirms registration. The account beneficiary must exactly match the company name as set out in the notarized deed.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Deed and Articles of Association
Passports of persons authorized to operate the account
Beneficial ownership declaration (Form A-like declaration per Swiss AML rules)
Bank account application for an escrow (Sperrkonto)
Proof of origin of funds (for AML purposes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC clarification, provide certified copies of the notarized deed and source-of-wealth evidence; select a different Swiss bank if refusal is final, then re-block the capital accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Application for Commercial Register Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) through eGRIS electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application with the notarized deed, bank block confirmation, and signed board declaration confirming directors' identities and representation authority. The filing must include the company's registered office, purpose, share capital, paid-up capital, and director lists. The registrar performs a formal legal review and issues a decision; upon approval the company acquires legal personality under OR 643.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Deed and Articles of Association
Confirmation of paid-up capital from the Swiss bank (Sperrkonto confirmation)
Board of Directors' declaration of compliance and capacity
Identification documents and signature specimens of each director
Application form of the Commercial Register (completed via eGRIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues queries or deficiencies, amend the articles or declarations within the stated deadline (usually 30 days) and resubmit through the notary; any exceeding of deadline requires renewed notarization and re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB), operated by the Federal Official Publications Center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register automatically transmits the registration to the SOGC for publication. The excerpt contains the company name, legal form, registered office, purpose, paid-in capital, and directors. Publication is a statutory condition for third-party reliance; the company's legal existence is effective as of the registration, and the SOGC notice confirms the formation usages.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register registration decision number
Notarized deed excerpt (issued by the notary)
Registration application confirmation (eGRIS receipt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication text contains an error in the company name or amount of paid-up capital, request a correction order from the Commercial Register; corrections are published retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Registration and Post-Registration Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton; Federal Tax Administration (FTA) for UID number; Cantonal Tax Authority for direct taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, request an official excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) evidencing the AG's existence. Apply for the Swiss UID number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) via the FTA's automated system. For purposes of VAT registration, confirm whether annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; if yes, register for VAT in a separate filing. The bank will release the escrow funds after receiving the registered excerpt.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt (updated)
Directors' passport copies
Registration notification from SHAB publication
FTA UID application form
VAT registration form (MWST/Formulaire 106 or online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID application is rejected due to missing source document, upload the certified Commercial Register excerpt and re-submit via the FTA's online portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: For distribution and warehousing activities under ISIC 4652, no industry-specific industrial manufacturing license is required; the relevant authorities are the Cantonal Building Inspectorate (for building and storage permits) and the Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU) for environmental aspects
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General business/occupancy permit for the warehouse and office premises, including a fire safety approval for the storage of electronic components, where applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU) in coordination with the Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required for passive electronic component distribution and warehousing; exempt from a full EIA. If the operation includes a new warehouse building or storage of goods exceeding waste or emission thresholds, a preliminary screening under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (VPVP) may be required at the cantonal level.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges are expected; wastewater from sanitary facilities and cleaning must comply with the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) Annex 2.1 thresholds. VOC emissions from stored components must remain below the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) concentration limits for storage facilities. Waste handling of electronic scrap, if any, must comply with the Ordinance on Movements of Waste (VeVA) and reporting obligations to BAFU.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the cantonal fire prevention authority (Feuerpolizei) confirming adequate extinguishing systems, evacuation routes, and storage distances; structural load approval for racking and shelving systems from the building inspector; occupational safety clearance issued or accepted by the Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA) covering workplace safety and health protection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern; self-service portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration and filing via ESTV’s SUISA/MWST portal and e-service suite.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not resident in Switzerland that makes taxable supplies in Switzerland or imports goods subject to Swiss VAT must register as a taxable person. The foreign principal must apply to the ESTV by written or electronic form and, unless exempted, appoint a fiscal representative resident in Switzerland for VAT purposes. Application requires proof of foreign registration, business purpose, expected turnover, and representative mandate. The ESTV assigns a Swiss VAT ID (MWST-Nr/IDE) after verification. Prior corporate income tax registration is not triggered solely by passive inventory distribution unless a Swiss permanent establishment is created.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. An Aktiengesellschaft is, by default, a fully taxable legal entity subject to federal, cantonal, and communal profit tax on worldwide income with unilateral credit, subject to Swiss territorial limitations for foreign permanent establishments and real estate. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are constrained by the Swiss general anti-abuse rules and the 2020 Multilateral Instrument; no elective hybrid mismatch regime exists. Group taxation is limited to the Swiss tax unity concept (Tragfähigkeitsprinzip) under specific cantonal/ordinary federal rules, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / TVA / IVA / MWST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (CHF 100,000 principal threshold; reduced thresholds for charities and certain nonprofit supplies); foreign suppliers may have mandatory registration from first taxable supply in Switzerland if not covered by threshold relief.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Swiss VAT does not require real-time government clearance or digital stamping. Taxable persons must issue invoices containing prescribed mandatory particulars; QR-bill (Swiss QR-IBC) and e-invoice formats satisfy documentation requirements. Since 2024, structured electronic invoicing is accepted but not obligatory unless parties agree. VAT returns are filed electronically through ESTV’s secure platform; no continuous transaction controls are in force. Import VAT is collected via the Swiss customs system and may be declared in the periodic VAT return under the import VAT settlement procedure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supply of goods qualifies for the 0% Swiss VAT rate if the goods are physically exported to a foreign destination by the supplier or a third party on behalf of the supplier, and the export is covered by customs documentation. Supply of services is zero-rated where the recipient is located abroad in accordance with Articles 23(2)/24 Swiss VAT Act, including services physically performed abroad, supplies of rights and immaterial goods to foreign recipients, and ancillary services to exports. Passive inventory distribution of electronic components qualifies if title risk passes abroad and the goods leave Swiss customs territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss export declaration/export customs declaration (Ausfuhrdeklaration) or certified alternative proof of customs transit
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical transport from Switzerland
Commercial invoice and sales contract referencing ISIC 4652 passive component supplies
Evidence of receipt by foreign recipient (delivery confirmation, import acceptance, or forwarding agent certificate)
Inward remittance certificate or payment evidence only where tax administration requires proof of consideration; Swiss practice permits bank transfer records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unjustified zero-rating is treated as tax evasion or attempted tax evasion under Articles 96-99 Swiss VAT Act. Interest at 4-5% per annum applies retroactively from the filing date, and penalties may reach up to three times the evaded tax; aggravated cases may be referred to criminal courts. Failure to substantiate export documentation within the statutory retention period (10 years) leads to reassessment at the standard 8.1% rate with reclaimable input tax denied, and late filing fines and administrative sanctions can additionally apply. ESTV audits export substantiation files routinely, including third-party customs data, transport tracking, and payment flows.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank; statutory basis: Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank (National Bank Act, NBG, SR 951.1) together with the SNB Survey Ordinance and related statistical reporting regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully convertible, freely floating currency regime with no legal distinction between current and capital account transactions. There are no licensing, approval, or prior-authorisation requirements for cross-border fund transfers, dividend remittances, loan principal payments, or repatriation of invested capital. The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully deliverable in both spot and forward markets. The only practical hurdles in profit remittance are fiscal in nature rather than exchange-control based, namely the Swiss dividend withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) at a standard rate of 35%, reduced or refundable under applicable double taxation treaties and subject to the rules on substantial participation, and the absence of any requirement to obtain a commercial bank or SNB permission. Creditor protection rules under the Swiss Code of Obligations (e.g., capital preservation for distributions out of paid-in capital under Articles 671 and 675 OR) apply independently of currency transfer legality.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender regime in Switzerland. Exporters are not required to convert foreign currency receipts into CHF, have no mandatory timeline for repatriation, and may freely retain export proceeds in foreign currency accounts at Swiss banks or abroad. The only binding obligations are statistical: enterprises with material cross-border assets or liabilities must report to the Swiss National Bank under the SNB survey framework, and all cross-border payment instructions routed through Swiss banks are captured by the banks' mandatory reporting responsibilities to the SNB. No surrender ratio, waiting period, or conversion mandate applies.

Operational Account (CHF/EUR multi-currency, e-banking and cash-pooling)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Julius Bär Group AG (Bank Julius Bär & Co. Ltd.)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account only if paired with a wealth-management mandate; not suitable for transactional treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury relationship, Medium as an ancillary payments channel. An offshore digital EMI or electronic money institution that is not licensed or recognised by FINMA may not lawfully take deposits or maintain a resident Swiss transactional account; deposit-taking from Swiss persons triggers Banking Act licensing or the FinTech licence under Article 1b of the Banking Act (deposits capped at CHF 100 million). Cross-border EMIs (e.g., UK or EU licensed providers) may be used for virtual-IBAN receivable collection, expense cards, or payout aggregation if the commercial risk is accepted, but all final CHF clearing and corporate liquidity must be held and settled with a FINMA-licensed bank connected to the SIC/euroSIC system. Legal constraints include the Swiss Financial Institutions Act (FinIA), the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), and the requirement that any payment service offered to Swiss customers be operationally anchored in a Swiss-regulated institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss law does not impose an absolute requirement of physical appearance. Under the AMLA and FINMA regulation, banks may perform client identification through an audited process, including video-identification and electronic signature systems. In practice, however, tier-1 universal banks such as UBS and Zürcher Kantonalbank generally require at least one physical interview in Switzerland with the authorized signatories and the ultimate beneficial owner, or, where remote application is permitted, a documented video call followed by apostilled and certified corporate documents and validation against the Swiss commercial register (Handelsregister). If the ultimate beneficial owner is resident in a non-DTA or high-risk jurisdiction, physical presence is effectively mandatory. Directors may fulfil part of the process remotely only when a qualified Swiss-based AML officer, fiduciary, or banking attorney is engaged to authenticate the transaction. The default onboarding standard for a newly formed CH_AG should assume a physical sign-off at the bank or at a Swiss notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indirect or nominee ownership structure where the ultimate beneficial owner is not a Swiss tax resident and the shareholding chain passes through a multi-layer intermediate holding entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current commercial register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) issued within 30 days; apostilled certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing from the home jurisdiction; complete beneficial ownership declaration (Form A / Form I) identifying each natural person owning 25% or more; notarized board resolution authorizing the opening; group structure chart; audited source-of-funds file for the capital contribution, including stamped bank confirmation and the underlying agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity or payment volume inconsistent with the declared share capital and the operating profile of a passive electronics distributor (e.g., high invoice counts with low unit values, or cross-border payments that are disproportionate to inventory levels).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited statutory financial statements (Article 727 OR) or interim management accounts; ISIC 4652 business plan; warehouse lease agreement and inventory custody evidence; supplier and customer master files; ERP extract of inventory movements; sample transaction file comprising commercial invoices, packing lists, CMR / bill of lading, and customs declarations proving genuine goods flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparties domiciled in non-FATF-compliant or high-risk jurisdictions, or settlement routed through third-party payment agents and receivables purchase intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty know-your-customer questionnaire; group AML risk classification memorandum; UCP 600 documentary credit package (when applicable), including the underlying purchase order, transport document, and certificate of origin; final downstream sale invoice or reseller evidence; SWIFT gpi MT199 payment tracking reports evidencing the full chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of assigned receivables, factoring, or payables-finance arrangements with offshore financiers creating ambiguity about the true beneficiary of payments, or mismatch between invoice currency and settlement currency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assignment of claims register and notice of subordination; debt purchase or payables finance agreement; treasury policy memorandum restricting FX conversion to the clearing bank; reconciliation report between invoices, receivables ledger, and bank statements; ISDA master agreement if derivative hedging is added; sanction-screening evidence aligned with SECO and FINMA lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections are made by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for bank-to-bank cover) in CHF, EUR, or USD to the CH_AG's account at a SIC participant. The payment instruction shall carry an explicit purpose reference (Zahlungszweck), for example 'Kapitalerhöhung' (capital increase), 'Agio' (share premium), or 'Gesellschafterdarlehen' (shareholder loan) to support accounting treatment and, if applicable, the capital escrow attestation. No SNB permit or exchange-control approval is required. Inbound funds are credited immediately once the bank validates the beneficiary name and account. The board resolution, notarial deed for the share-capital increase (where registered capital is increased), and, if applicable, the shareholder loan agreement must be retained. Where the aggregate external assets and liabilities of the enterprise exceed the SNB statistical thresholds, the receiving bank will automatically forward the transaction to the SNB for balance-of-payments and external-asset statistics; no separate filing is required by the customer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade funding for inventory purchases of capacitors and resistors should be executed through (i) direct SWIFT MT103 transfers for open-account settlement, with a payment purpose code describing 'purchase of electronic components' and full beneficiary bank detail; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600, with the Swiss bank acting as issuing or confirming bank, particularly when dealing with Asian and emerging-market suppliers; and (iii) SEPA credit transfers in EUR for counterparties located in the European Economic Area and participating SEPA countries. Domestic Swiss payments are cleared through the SIC system or QR-bill payments. All international transactions run through SWIFT with the bank performing sanctions screening against SECO, FINMA, and international (OFAC/UN) lists. Supplier disbursements may be accelerated through bank-guaranteed receivables and supply-chain finance agreements that are expressly documented with the clearing bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forwards (FXA) on CHF/EUR and CHF/USD under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex, executed only with FINMA-regulated counterparties
FX swaps (swap points roll-over) for short-dated working-capital currency funding on CHF/EUR and CHF/USD legs
Vanilla European-style FX options, either bought or sold with a documented hedge rationale, to protect inventory-backed cash flows from adverse CHF movements
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to align the currency of committed credit-line debt with the functional currency of the balance sheet

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely where an underlying trade leg references a non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currency; no NDF is necessary or advisable for CHF itself given full deliverability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts, audit or limited-review report, and AGM approval minutes (Jahresrechnung, Revisionsbericht, Generalversammlung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders; copies filed with the combined federal/cantonal tax return and kept at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM within six months after balance-sheet date; for a 31-December year-end by 30 June (Art. 698 para. 3 Swiss Code of Obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court admonition and fines up to CHF 10,000 for failure to keep or file statutory accounts (StGB Art. 325; CO Art. 920a); persistent non-compliance can trigger court-ordered liquidation and deletion from the Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual federal, cantonal and communal corporate income tax and capital tax return (Steuererklärung) with annual accounts attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Office (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 June following the 31-December tax year; extension routinely granted by the canton up to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential default assessment based on the authorities' own estimate, late-payment interest at 4.5–5.0% p.a., and procedural fines up to CHF 10,000; administrative deletion only after insolvency proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and annual reconciliation (Mehrwertsteuerabrechnung) under the Swiss federal VAT Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration – VAT Division (ESTV/FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the VAT year for the combined fourth-quarter return and annual reconciliation; semi-annual filers due within 60 days of each period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT reminder fees, default assessment with statutory interest at 4.5% p.a., and escalating fines for repeated or deliberate failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register notifications of AGM appointments, board changes, share-capital mutations or other registry updates (no annual return for an unchanged private AG)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) with SHAB gazette publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediately after the relevant AGM or board resolution; not an anniversary-based annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for late or incorrect registration; the register office can issue a formal warning and, if unresolved, initiate ex officio dissolution; Switzerland does not apply an automatic annual strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit is mandatory if the AG exceeds two of the following three thresholds on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: CHF 20 million total assets, CHF 40 million gross turnover, or 250 average full-time employees. Smaller AGs require a limited audit (eingeschränkte Revision) unless the shareholders pass an annual opt-out resolution, which is allowed only when the company has no more than 10 average full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting law (Art. 957–963a); Swiss GAAP FER is the standard local framework; IFRS is permitted and customary for internationally active groups but mandatory only for listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no public UBO register for private AGs. The Board must annually review the Register of Members, obtain written ownership declarations identifying every natural person holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights, ensure bearer shares (if any) are held through a regulated depositary or converted to registered shares, and minute the confirmation at the AGM. As a goods trader, the AG is also subject to Swiss Anti-Money-Laundering Act due diligence for counterparties in non-routine cash or otherwise unusual transactions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors / Board resolution minutes (Verwaltungsratsprotokoll)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,700 – 4,300 (CHF 1,500 – 3,800) per year for registered office, corporate secretariat and registered agent services in Zug or Geneva
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,900 – 9,200 (CHF 2,500 – 8,000) for a limited statutory audit/review; USD 11,500 – 34,000 (CHF 10,000 – 30,000) for a full ordinary statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax on post-tax profit (equivalent to approx. 7.83% on a pre-tax basis); combined rate in the canton of Zug approx. 11.9% (4.2% federal plus 7.7% cantonal and communal); combined effective statutory range across Switzerland approx. 11% to 21% depending on canton and communal multiplier
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland grants no general tax holidays; the 2020 Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF) provides: cantonal patent box with up to 90% exemption of qualifying patent and comparable income, R&D super-deduction of 125% to 150% of qualifying expenditure, notional interest deduction (NID) on surplus qualifying equity, and the federal participation relief exempting qualifying inter-corporate dividend income from effective taxation; total relief is statutorily capped so that at least 30% to 70% of taxable profit remains in the assessment base per canton

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal-federal corporate tax return 'Steuererklaerung juristische Personen' (Form 201 / Form 30 AG schedules; annexes: schedule A statistics of income, schedule B balance sheet, schedule C tax adjustments), filed electronically via the cantonal e-filing portal of Zug (eSteuer / TaxCockpit interface) and the ESTV Steuererklarung portal for federal direct tax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the combined return is due 31 May to 30 June of the following year depending on canton, with a written extension ordinarily granted until 31 October; Federal Direct Tax Act (DBG) Art. 124 confirms the statutory filing obligation running in parallel with the cantonal return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales revenue from distribution of excess multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors (ISIC 4652 trading margin)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only sales attributable to a Swiss permanent establishment; if the AG is owned non-resident, all worldwide sales of the Swiss resident AG must be declared in full

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, inbound logistics, warehousing and freight expenses related to electronic component trading
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply arm's-length allocation of group logistics costs; no deduction for internally generated goodwill or for payments to non-resident related parties exceeding arm's-length value

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit (Reingewinn) per the Swiss audited annual financial statements prepared under Swiss Code of Obligations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG files as a Swiss tax resident; a non-resident branch would file a separate Swiss branch P&L allocating profit to the Swiss PE only

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments (Hinzurechnungen) per DBG Art. 57 and 58: add-back of hidden profit distributions, excessive royalties, non-arm's-length interest or management fees, and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure all intercompany charges are supported by written contracts and OECD-compliant benchmarking; failing this the tax authorities reclassify the excess as a taxable hidden dividend

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) for qualifying dividends from participations of at least 10% held for at least 12 months
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Swiss resident AG can claim the relief on its own dividend income; relief is unavailable on distributions received by non-resident shareholders

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Utilisation of available loss carryforwards (maximum 7 years, no carryback) against current-year taxable profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Swiss PE of a non-resident company may utilise only the PE's own loss carryforward; losses of the foreign head office are not deductible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable equity capital for cantonal/communal capital tax purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The equity figure is the statutory Swiss balance-sheet equity after revaluations; no treaty relief applies to capital tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a Verspaetungszuschlag (late-filing surcharge) of up to 10% of the assessed tax or a fixed fine of CHF 500; the federal administration may impose administrative fines up to CHF 30,000; unpaid taxes accrue interest at 4.5% p.a.; deliberate concealment triggers tax-evasion penalties of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividend distributions under Art. 1 of the Withholding Tax Act (VStG)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss AG withholds 35% at source; the non-resident shareholder must file a refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) using Form 823 (or Form 824 for countries without a DTA) within 3 years after the calendar year of distribution; the claim must be accompanied by a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority; for a qualifying EU parent company holding at least 25% of the Swiss AG for at least 2 years, the dividend bears 0% Swiss WHT under the Swiss-EU Parent-Subsidiary arrangement; standard DTA relief reduces the rate to 5% for qualifying substantial holdings (e.g., 25% for China, 10% for US) and to 15% for portfolio holdings
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss internal law imposes no withholding tax on arm's-length royalties or ordinary cross-border debt interest; the only exception concerns interest on Swiss-issued bonds and money-market instruments where the bank is a Swiss payer; under the Swiss-EU Agreement on interest and royalties of 26 October 2004, qualifying associated EU enterprises obtain 0% withholding on both royalties and interest; bilateral DTAs generally suppress any residual source taxation to 0-10% for royalties and 5-10% for interest

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File apply to Swiss group members of multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of CHF 900 million or more, effective for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2020 (ESTV TP documentation circular of 2021); below that threshold no standing documentation is mandatory, but the taxpayer must be able to produce transfer pricing documentation, benchmarking studies and intercompany contracts within 30 days of a tax audit request; a de minimis safe harbour exists for annual controlled transactions below CHF 10 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies a rigorous economic-substance doctrine rather than a standalone ESR registration system; under TRAF 2020 and the ESTV royalty/substance doctrine, the Swiss AG must maintain a real physical office, qualified operational staff, independent management discretion, and actual risk-bearing functions in Switzerland to claim treaty benefits, patent-box relief, notional interest deductions, or to avoid reclassification as a shell holding vehicle; pure pass-through or nominee structures are rebutted, treaty relief is denied retroactively, and hidden profit distribution adjustments apply

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful submission of inaccurate books, books containing false entries, or omission of taxable distribution income in the Swiss AG annual return; e.g., under-reporting the resale margin on electronic components by routing sales through an undisclosed foreign nominee
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the evaded tax plus a penalty of 1 to 3 times the evaded amount (DBG Art. 175); default interest at 4.5% p.a.; criminal fine up to CHF 30,000; in aggravated cases custodial sentence up to 3 years under DBG Art. 186
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are personally liable as principals or accomplices; the corporate veil is pierced for civil restitution of the evaded tax, personal criminal records are imposed, non-resident directors may face preventive arrest or exit restrictions during criminal proceedings, and imprisonment is possible in severe cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-arm's-length consideration to shareholders or their affiliates, such as inflated royalties for IP, excessive management fees, interest-free loans, or artificial margins on intercompany component trade, thereby reducing Swiss taxable profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the excess as a dividend: additional tax assessment, 35% withholding tax on the constructive dividend with interest, and a negligence or evasion penalty of up to 3 times the additional tax; the hidden distribution is not deductible at either federal or cantonal level
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Art. 12 VStG the board of directors is jointly and severally liable with the company for the withheld but unpaid 35% tax unless each director proves absence of fault; the company may claim restitution against the directors under company law, and a criminal conviction triggers personal asset seizure and potential bankruptcy proceedings against director estates

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as a mailbox entity without premises, staff, or real decision-making, while routing cross-border royalties, dividends, or component invoices through Switzerland solely to obtain treaty benefits; use of nominee directors or purely passive electronic inventory ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief with retroactive full 35% withholding on all distributions; reassessment of income with imputed notional profit; penalties of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax for taxpayers; civil fines up to CHF 500,000 under anti-money-laundering rules for concealed beneficial ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors risk personal liability under the Swiss Code of Obligations for organizational deficits, disqualification from board service, criminal liability for negligent supervision under Art. 102 of the Swiss Criminal Code, and freeze or seizure of personal bank accounts if treaty abuse is held to be intentional fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, constructive dividends, or repatriating profits without withholding 35% to the ESTV, or failing to remit withheld amounts within the statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company must pay the full 35% from its own funds plus a 5% administrative surcharge and interest at 4.5% p.a.; failure to pay triggers criminal proceedings with fines up to 3 times the unpaid tax and potential imprisonment of the responsible signatory in aggravated cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members are personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax under Art. 12 VStG; civil execution may reach directors' personal assets, and criminal default sentences may include travel bans, house arrest, or imprisonment; directors who knowingly ordered the non-payment face criminal conviction as co-principals
